title: Haldane-Holstein model at fractional filling: Route to bosonic fractional Chern insulator and quantum anomalous Hall crystal
authors: Zezhu Wei, Ang-Kun Wu, Di Xiao, Shi-Zeng Lin
abstract: Electron-phonon coupling is generally expected to suppress band topology, driving a topological band insulator into a trivial phase. Here we show that, using the prototypical Haldane-Holstein model at partial filling of a topological band, strong electron-phonon coupling can instead stabilize topological phases of matter. The electron-phonon coupling plays a double role: it generates the longer-range interactions that correlate the carriers and, in the attractive channel, also binds them into bosonic pairs. For spinful electrons, it pairs opposite spins into charge-$2e$ bipolarons that form a bosonic fractional Chern insulator (FCI) at filling $ν=1/2$ with charge-$e$ semionic excitations. Tuning the band topology and the coupling strength maps out a rich phase diagram containing this bosonic FCI, superconductors condensed at the $M$ and $K$ points, and several charge-ordered solids. For spin-polarized electrons, strong coupling instead stabilizes a $C=2$ quantum anomalous Hall crystal (QAHC) at $ν=1/3$. Electron-phonon coupling thus emerges as a route to, rather than an obstruction against, topology in partially filled Chern bands.
summary: This work demonstrates that strong electron-phonon coupling can be a mechanism for stabilizing topological order rather than destroying it in partially filled Chern bands. By analyzing the Haldane-Holstein model, the authors predict the emergence of a bosonic Fractional Chern Insulator and a Quantum Anomalous Hall Crystal. The findings establish electron-phonon coupling as a route to topological matter in correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates how strong electron-phonon coupling can stabilize topological phases in partially filled Chern bands, contrary to the expectation that such coupling generally suppresses band topology.
main_result: Strong coupling stabilizes a bosonic Fractional Chern Insulator (FCI) at $\nu=1/2$ and a $C=2$ Quantum Anomalous Hall Crystal (QAHC) at $\nu=1/3$ for spin-polarized electrons.
method: The analysis employs the strong-coupling limit of the Haldane-Holstein model, utilizing Lang-Firsov transformations and subsequent effective boson Hamiltonians derived via degenerate perturbation theory.
model_or_system: The system is the Haldane-Holstein model at partial filling, which is analyzed by mapping the physics onto an effective hard-core boson model for bipolarons (charge-$2e$).
key_observables: Many-body Chern number ($C_{tot}$), superfluid stiffness ($\rho_{xx}^s$), and the existence of quantized Hall conductance ($\sigma_{xy} = 2e^2/h$).
important_parameters: The dimensionless electron-phonon coupling parameter $X = U_{ph}/\omega$, and the effective interaction-to-hopping ratio $\kappa$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the strong-coupling limit, and the effective Hamiltonians are derived using perturbation theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram of the effective boson Hamiltonian showing FCI, solid phases, and superconductors; other figures detail the band folding and Chern number calculation for the QAHC state.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and the role of electron-phonon coupling. It then derives the effective boson Hamiltonian in the strong-coupling limit. The results map out a rich phase diagram showing the FCI and QAHC states, followed by detailed analysis of the charge fractionalization and band folding mechanisms.
why_interesting: The mechanism by which lattice coupling (phonons) can induce and stabilize exotic topological states (FCI, QAHC) by mediating strong correlations is highly relevant to understanding emergent topological phases in strongly correlated materials.
